breakdown.phrase: needs a medium amount of irrigation water
has a low risk of heat, cold and frost damage
leaves the soil bare for long stretches (erosion risk)
needs a lot of nitrogen fertilizer

explain.summary: Corn · Corn · Corn is place 221 of 225 tested rotations with your weights. Its strongest point: it has a low risk of heat, cold and frost damage. Its weakest point: it needs a lot of nitrogen fertilizer.
explain.note: Scores compare the 225 tested rotations with each other (0 = best, 1 = worst). They are not an absolute grade and not a promise of yield or profit.

caveats.text: Scores compare the 225 tested rotations with each other (0 = best, 1 = worst). They are not an absolute grade and not a promise of yield or profit.
Nitrogen amounts in pounds are not in the data yet, only the nitrogen score is. A missing amount does not mean zero.
Yields, irrigation and stress values are model results based on past weather (1991-2025). They are not forecasts.
Weather comes from a coarse grid (about 50 km), not from a station at your field.
An effect of the crop order comes from a study or guide from another region (Seifert, Roberts & Lobell 2017, Agron. J. 109(2):541 (summary: UNL CropWatch 2020)). Treat it as a rough guide.

assumptions.text: The crop before the first season comes from satellite crop maps (USDA CDL), not from your own records.
The year of the first sowing is assumed, not chosen by you.
The irrigation level of each season (full) is an assumption, not your own choice.
Cold stress is our own rule (below the crop's best temperature for at least half a day), not a standard threshold.
